topic: Task-Based versus Thread-Based: Offloading Management via std::async
explanation: The core design principle of `std::async` is to shift the onus of complex thread management—including avoiding oversubscription, handling thread pooling, and managing resource limits—from the application developer to the Standard Library implementation. This delegation significantly reduces the likelihood of encountering resource exhaustion errors (like out-of-threads exceptions) and allows the library to make better, platform-specific decisions about concurrency execution than a developer could manually hardcode.
code_example: auto fut = std::async (doAsyncWork); // Thread management is handled by the library implementation.
practical_example: A microservice needs to execute hundreds of concurrent tasks. If raw `std::thread` is used, the developer must implement a thread pool to prevent system resource exhaustion. By using `std::async`, the library handles the pooling logic, ensuring efficient utilization without risking an OS-level thread limit exception.
chapter: Item 35: Prefer task-based programming to thread-based
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
